elements.evidence: Rendered § 12.4 now reads in full: "Customer is subject to no non-solicitation restriction under this Agreement." The prior eighteen-month solicit/engage covenant binding Customer is gone, and § 12.3 (retained) independently confirms Customer has made "no ... no-hire commitment" and may hire persons responding to general recruitment, so no residual restriction on Customer survives anywhere in the cited text.

Vacuously satisfied: the operative text eliminates the non-solicitation covenant entirely, so there is no one-sided restriction binding Customer for the mutuality condition to apply. The fallback's premise (an existing restriction) does not exist after the edit.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: no restriction remains, so the former "any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term" scope is removed and no over-broad personnel coverage subsists.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the eighteen-month post-termination period is deleted and no duration remains to exceed 12 months.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: with no restriction, no carve-out is needed; § 12.3 separately preserves Customer's freedom to hire "any person who responds to general recruitment."

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: there is no covenant that could capture an unsolicited approach by a Vendor employee.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The word "engage" (the effective no-hire) is removed with the whole covenant; § 12.3's acknowledgement of "no ... no-hire commitment" is retained and now consistent rather than in tension with § 12.4.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single-sentence replacement of § 12.4 leaves Customer with no non-solicitation obligation, which is the sole preferred element.
Fallback elements are vacuously met because the redline removes the restriction altogether; no restriction exists to be non-mutual, over-broad, over-long, no-hire, or lacking carve-outs.

Minimality holds: only § 12.4 is touched, by one surgical replacement sentence; § 12.3 and all other language are retained verbatim, and no survival tail, procedure, or extra obligation is added. Stating the result affirmatively rather than deleting the section preserves the numbering and avoids a dangling § 12.4 reference, so it is not a cosmetic extra.

Intent is preserved: the edit removes the internal tension with § 12.3 (which already recites that Customer made no no-hire commitment) rather than creating one; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references result, and no Vendor-side rights, timing, or remedies elsewhere are disturbed.

The margin comment correctly states the playbook position and offers the narrow mutual fallback without importing it into operative text, which is the right treatment (a fallback promised only in a comment cannot count as operative language, and here it is not relied on).
